User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user profile within the Finnovate application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user's avatar image.

joinedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user joined the application.

parentConsent.description: Indicates whether parental consent has been given (if required).

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a financial transaction for a user.

merchant.description: The merchant associated with the transaction.

category.description: The category of the transaction (e.g., Food, Transport).

type.description: The type of transaction (debit or credit).

source.description: The source of the transaction (manual or sync).

Goal.title: Goal
Goal.description: Represents a savings goal for a user.

title.description: The title of the savings goal.

targetAmount.description: The target amount for the savings goal.

currentAmount.description: The current amount saved towards the goal.

deadline.description: The deadline for achieving the savings goal.

isLinked.description: Indicates whether the goal is linked to a real transfer.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the goal was created.

visualColor.description: The visual color associated with the goal.

Wallet.title: Wallet
Wallet.description: Represents a virtual wallet for a user.

Quest.title: Quest
Quest.description: Represents a quest assigned to a user.

status.description: The status of the quest (e.g., active, completed).

claimedReward.description: Indicates whether the reward for the quest has been claimed.

QuestTemplate.title: QuestTemplate
QuestTemplate.description: Represents a template for a quest.

id.description: Unique identifier for the quest template.

name.description: The name of the quest template.

description.description: The description of the quest template.

reward.description: The reward for completing the quest.

imageUrl.description: The URL of the badge image.

LeaderboardEntry.title: LeaderboardEntry
LeaderboardEntry.description: Represents an entry in a leaderboard.

period.description: The period for the leaderboard (e.g., weekly, monthly).

score.description: The score of the user in the leaderboard.

startDate.description: The start date of the challenge.

endDate.description: The end date of the challenge.

SimulatorPosition.title: SimulatorPosition
SimulatorPosition.description: Represents a position in the investment simulator.

id.description: Unique identifier for the simulator position.

ticker.description: The ticker symbol of the asset.

quantity.description: The quantity of the asset held.

purchasePrice.description: The purchase price of the asset.

purchaseDate.description: The date the asset was purchased.

MoodEntry.title: MoodEntry
MoodEntry.description: Represents a mood entry logged by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the mood entry.

mood.description: The mood of the user (e.g., happy, sad).

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the mood entry.

note.description: An optional note associated with the mood entry.

NudgeLog.title: NudgeLog
NudgeLog.description: Represents a log of nudges sent to a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the nudge log entry.

nudgeType.description: The type of nudge sent (e.g., budget rebalance).

timestamp.description: The timestamp when the nudge was sent.

firestore.reasoning:
Based on the user's request to connect everything user-wise and the provided data entities, the recommended Firestore structure focuses on nesting data under user documents to ensure data locality and simplified security rules. This approach aligns with the principle of path-based ownership and enables efficient querying of user-specific data.

**Authorization Independence:**
All subcollections under `/users/{userId}` inherit authorization from the user document itself, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules. The `userId` field in each subcollection document explicitly links the data to the user, making authorization independent of parent document content. For collaborative data, the membership map approach is not required, as ownership is implicit via the path.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   The structure supports secure `list` operations for user-specific data because all documents within a subcollection share the same security context (the user's ID). This allows rules to validate that `request.auth.uid == userId` without needing to filter based on document content.
*   Public data such as `QuestTemplate`, `Badge`, and `Challenge` is segregated into separate collections, allowing for different security rules (e.g., read access for all users). Leaderboard entries do not contain any private user data and are handled separately.

This structure promotes clarity, security, and efficient data retrieval, while adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates.
